statement.p: Compute the surface integral over the given oriented surface:
\mathbf{F}=y^{3} \mathbf{i}+7 \mathbf{j}-x \mathbf{k},\quad portion of the plane x+y+z=1 in the octant x, y, z \ge 0,\quad downward-pointing normal

static.solution:
We parametrize the surface by: \mathrm{\Phi }( x,y )=( x,y,1-x-y ), using the parameter domain \mathcal{D} shown in the figure.
Step 1. Compute the tangent and normal vectors.
We have: {\mathbf{T} }_x = \frac{\partial \mathrm{\Phi}}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(x,y,1-x-y) = \left\lt 1,0,-1 \right> {\mathbf{T} }_y = \frac{\partial\mathrm{\Phi}}{\partial y}=\frac{\partial}{\partial y}(x,y,1-y) = \left\lt 0,1,-1 \right> {\mathbf{T} }_x \times {\mathbf{T} }_y = \left|\begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} \amp \mathbf{j} \amp \mathbf{k} \\1\amp 0\amp -1\\0\amp 1\amp -1 \end{array}\right| = \mathbf{i} +\mathbf{j} +\mathbf{k} = \left\lt 1,1,1 \right> Since the normal points downward, the z-component must be negative, hence: \mathbf{n} = \left\lt -1,-1,-1 \right> Step 2. Evaluate the dot product \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n}.
We compute the dot product: \mathbf{F} \left(\mathrm{\Phi}(x,y)\right)\cdot \mathbf{n} = \left\lt y^{3},7,-x \right>\cdot \left\lt -1,-1,-1 \right> = -y^{3}-{7}+x Step 3. Evaluate the surface integral.
The surface integral is equal to the following double integral: \iint_S \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = \iint_{\mathcal{D}} \mathbf{F} \left(\mathrm{\Phi}(x,y)\right) \cdot \mathbf{n} \,dx \,dy=\int_0^1 \int_0^{1-y} \left(-y^{3}-{7}+x\right) \,dx \,dy= \int_0^1 -y^{3}x-{7}x+\frac{x^2}{2}\bigg|_{x=0}^{1-y} \,dy= \int_0^1 \left(-y^{3}(1-y)-{7}(1-y)+\frac{{(1-y)}^2}{2}\right) \,dy=\int_0^1 \left(y^{4}-y^{3}+{7}(y-1)+\frac{{(y-1)}^2}{2}\right) \,dy= \frac{y^{5}}{5}-\frac{y^{4}}{4}+{3.5}{(y-1)}^2+\frac{{(y-1)}^3}{6}\bigg|_0^1=\left(\frac1{5}-\frac1{4}\right)-\left(3.5-\frac16\right)= -3.38333
